## The two days

| Day | Topics | Slides |
|-----|--------|--------|
| 1 | Setup and help - packages and environments - NumPy - SciPy | [Day 1](#day-1) |
| 2 | pandas - Matplotlib - seaborn - scikit-learn - where to go next | [Day 2](#day-2) |

Each day runs **3 hours**, with a 10-minute break. Every block starts with a few minutes of slides, then exercises.

## Setup

1. Install [Miniforge](https://conda-forge.org/download/), which gives you `conda` with conda-forge as the default channel.
2. Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/#installing-uv).
3. Get the course materials: `git clone` the course repository, or [download](https://github.com/IgorTatarnikov/course-intro-scientific-python/archive/main.zip) it as a ZIP.
4. In a terminal, from the extracted or cloned course folder:

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate scientific-python
python check_setup.py
```

Every line should say `OK`.

## How the exercises work

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**In the repository**

- `notebooks/`: the exercises
- `solutions/`: worked solutions
- `data/`: every dataset we use, so nothing downloads during class
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**In class**

- Attempt each exercise before looking anything up
- Work with your neighbour
- Put up your hand (or a red sticky note) when stuck
:::
::::

## Where the material comes from

- **International Brain Laboratory, Brain Wide Map** [@ibl_bwm_dandi]: the Neuropixels recording every exercise is built on
- **Scientific Python Lectures** [@spl]: the NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib exercises, adapted to the recording
- **Software Carpentry gapminder lesson** [@swc_gapminder]: the pandas exercises, adapted to the recording, and the gapminder data on the slides
- **Python Data Science Handbook** [@pdsh]: background reading for NumPy, pandas and plotting

Material from these sources is adapted under their licences. See each notebook's header for details.
